headline.text: New Zealand election too close to call
headline.context: Luxon's coalition has a slim lead after the count.
headline.vo: New Zealand's election is too close to call. After Saturday's vote, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's coalition holds a razor-thin lead, but the final result is weeks away.

beats.vo: Luxon's National Party and Labour each won about twenty-nine percent of the party vote, AAP reports. The new Opportunity Party is set to enter parliament for the first time.

beats.label: of 130 seats for Luxon's coalition, preliminary results
beats.text: *66* seats are needed for a majority.
beats.vo: On preliminary results, National, ACT and New Zealand First would win sixty-seven seats. Parliament grows to one hundred and thirty seats, so sixty-six are needed for a majority. Special votes, including from overseas, are still to be counted.

beats.quote: But I have to tell you right now it is too close to call.
beats.vo: Labour leader Chris Hipkins did not concede. He said every vote must now be counted. The final result is due on November twenty-seventh.

title: New Zealand election too close to call as Luxon's coalition holds a slim lead
caption: New Zealand's general election ended without a clear winner. On preliminary results, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's coalition of National, ACT and NZ First would hold 67 of 130 seats, just above the 66 needed for a majority. Special votes are still being counted, and the final result is due on November 27.
